text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a non-review research study focused on the development and application of LUCAS, a spatially explicit state-and-transition simulation model for predicting future land use and land cover (LULC) change across the conterminous United States—meeting the national-scale criterion. The primary objective is LULC prediction integrated with carbon dynamics, but LULC change is central to the modeling framework. The study implements multiple future scenarios, including IPCC-SRES A1B, A2, B1, B2 and RCPs, enabling quantitative comparison. It uses spatially explicit modeling with 1-km resolution, includes mapped LULC projections (e.g., Figures 7A–B), and reports quantitative metrics such as area targets, net change by ecoregion (Table 4), and transition probabilities validated against input targets (Figure 6, R² > 0.99). Although carbon dynamics are included, LULC prediction is not merely an input—it is the core simulated process driving the analysis. All inclusion criteria are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.)
